subject: Culture
title: Birth Gifts Worldwide
description: A fast breakdown of Birth Gifts Worldwide for builders.

hook.text: Finland gives every newborn a cardboard box filled with baby supplies. The box doubles as the baby's first bed.

buildup.text: Birth gifts reinforce community bonds. African traditions send naming-ceremony gifts. Jewish families give silver cups.

discovery.text: In China, the 'full month' celebration one month after birth marks survival—historically the dangerous period.

twist.text: Finland's baby box program cut infant mortality dramatically. A practical gift became a life-saving policy.

climax.text: Birth gifts encode what a culture values most: silver says wealth, blankets say warmth, books say knowledge.

punchline.text: A baby's first gift reveals a society's deepest hope.

quiz.question: Which country gives every newborn a cardboard box of supplies?
